text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chairman of Bosnian presidency Alija Izetbegovic will visit Turkey on June 8 to meet Turkish President Suleiman Demirel and other officials, his aides said.

- If meeting between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and presidency chairman goes ahead by end of this month, it would mean the forming of a joint police force in Mostar area, Izetbegovic tells newspaper.
- Experts from Bosnia and Croatia discussed a proposal for seven land corridors linking the two countries which will be presented at an upcoming conference in Helsinki, officials say.

- Southern European Cooperation Initiative official says it will support a $1 billion project to build a new natural gas network which would connect Bosnia to a system linking Norway, Algeria (via Italy) and Britain.

- Governments of Bosnia's two entities, Moslem-Croat federation and Serb republic, have agreed to form a joint delegation for the upcoming international donors' conference this month. The delegation is due to present common projects in the metallurgy and energy sectors.
- Leaders of both entities also discussed an unresolved debt which has blocked the delivery of natural gas to the country, federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic said.
- The OSCE has extended a registration deadline for out-of-country voters until June 14, an OSCE spokesman says. The previous deadline for voter registration was June 7.

- Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Husein Zivalj criticises demand from Croatia to allow Croats in Bosnia to vote during Croatian presidential elections scheduled this month. Zivalj says this create "a diplomatic precedent" because an agreement on dual citizenship has yet to be signed by the two states. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
